summary: Leon walks through a vast, dim facility with Ria, who explains that Viktor, a giant entity controlled through tendrils, is weak inside this body and that a Mark II system is being built half a mile underground. Ria says the Mark I was jury-rigged after Viktor's accident, which she declines to describe, and she dismisses Leon's fears of assassination, harvesting or hunting. The passage ends as they pass through rooms, including one where Viktor's breath and circulation systems are housed, toward an airlock guarded by security.
one_line: Leon is guided by Ria through a secretive facility housing Viktor, a giant entity whose accident and new Mark II system remain mysterious.
key_facts: Ria tells Leon that Viktor has all the power in the world when contacted outside through his many tendrils or by phone, but is very, very weak inside his body.
Ria says the suits in the facility are there to level out the playing field and are described as all head-games and symbolism.
The system Leon is inside is called Mark I, which was jury-rigged after Viktor's accident.
The Mark II system is being built about five miles from the facility and half a mile underground.
When the Mark II is ready, a tunnel will be blasted and Viktor taken all the way down into it without compromising the skin of his extended body.
Leon says he assumed Viktor's condition was a stroke, and Ria replies, "Nothing like that."
The great room was left over from the original floor-plan, when the place was biotech R&D used for all-hands meetings and small symposiums.
Ria says security protocol dictates no more than ten people in any one space.
When Leon asks whether it was assassination, Ria answers simply, "No."
Ria says that if Viktor needed an organ, they would print one right there in about forty hours.
Ria calls the chance that Leon will be harvested or hunted "a very low probability outcome."
The rhythmic whoosh whoosh vibration coming through the floor is Viktor's breath, produced by filtration systems located below a service hatch.
Circulatory system tubes are bundled in troughs behind a grate in the ceiling of one room.
The passage ends at an airlock door guarded by a plainclothes security woman in front of a side-room full of people watching screens.
